title: Shuffle squares in smooth binary words and the Kolakoski sequence
summary: A binary word is a shuffle square if its positions can be partitioned into two identical subsequences. A finite word over $\{1,2\}$ is smooth if repeated finite run-length differentiation remains binary until the empty word is reached. This paper proves that every smooth binary word in which both letters have even multiplicity is a shuffle square once its length is at least $18$. There are exactly $34$ exceptions, all of length at most $16$.
